title: Computer vision
stage: College AI and machine learning degree
audience: a college student in an artificial intelligence, machine learning or computer science degree program, or an adult studying the same material on their own
purpose: Learn how machines see: images as arrays and color spaces, filtering and edge detection, features, convolutional networks for image classification, data augmentation, object detection with bounding boxes, intersection over union and non-maximum suppression, semantic and instance segmentation, vision transformers and self-supervised vision, image generation in brief, cameras and 3-D vision basics, and the robustness, bias and responsible use of vision systems.
primary_reading: Computer Vision: Algorithms and Applications, 2nd edition, by Richard Szeliski (free PDF)

weeks.1: Images as arrays: pixels, channels and color spaces
weeks.5: Data augmentation and training vision models
weeks.6: Object detection: bounding boxes and intersection over union
weeks.12: Robustness, bias and the responsible use of vision systems

blocks.deliverable: Apply filters to a small grayscale image by hand and in code.
Detect edges in a small image with Sobel filters.
Compute IoU for pairs of boxes.
Week 7 midterm; run non-maximum suppression on a list of detections.
Split an image into patches and compute patch embeddings.
Evaluate a model's accuracy across subgroups of a test set.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Shape detector: implement filtering, edge detection, a simple sliding-window or connected-component detector and non-maximum suppression in plain Python for supplied small grayscale images given as grids of numbers, evaluate it with IoU, precision and recall, and write a report on its failures and how a convolutional network would address them.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
